title: Slot-lease sidecar and bloom prefetch orbit for low-latency paged KV
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Our paged KV cache suffers from transient tail latency when large prefills contend with allocation and eviction on decode waves. Current allocation is tightly coupled to the kernel admission path which causes head-of-line stalls when a single tenant or long sequence prefill blocks allocator metadata updates.

Goal: Reduce 95/99th decode latency by decoupling short-duration slot leasing from the allocator core and by introducing a lightweight probabilistic prefetch service (the 'bloom orbit') that speculatively warms KV pages for likely soon-to-be-requested key spans without imposing synchronous allocation contention. Aim for 10-25% reduction in 99th tail latency on mixed workloads and measurable reduction in prefill-induced allocation spikes.

Design summary: Implement a slot-lease sidecar component that: (1) takes short-term soft leases on page slots (microseconds-to-seconds) without updating global allocation tables synchronously, (2) exposes a fast path to the decode subsystem to mark leased slots as reserved so kernels can prefill into them, and (3) reconciles leases with the allocator asynchronously, allowing the allocator to consolidate and persist allocations in a batched, low-priority pass.

Introduce the bloom prefetch orbit: a background worker attached to each shard that maintains a compact bloom filter-based hotset estimator derived from recent attention touch patterns and kernel-level hints. The orbit issues speculative prefill requests for key ranges with high probability, subject to a budget (bytes/sec and slot count). Prefetch decisions are soft — orbit prefills into leased slots and the sidecar marks them as warm but does not force eviction of high-priority residency.

Kernel selection & hinting: Add a lightweight kernel API extension (kernel_hint_t) that allows the decode/prefill pipeline to annotate requests with one of {LATENCY_SENSITIVE, BATCHABLE, PREFILL_HINT, KERNEL_FALLBACK}. The runtime's kernel selector will treat PREFILL_HINT as a lower-cost signal for orbit prioritization and LATENCY_SENSITIVE to favor immediate allocation finalization. This lets us route requests without coupling to synchronous allocation operations.
acceptance_criteria: 99th decode latency reduced by >=10% on mixed synthetic workload (long and short sequences)
Avg allocator metadata update rate decreased during prefill storms by >=30%
Orbit budget enforcement avoids >5% increase in evictions for tenant hotsets
No regression in correctness: KV content visible to decode path after prefill and reconciliation
Feature gated via runtime flag and can be disabled without requiring model restarts
implementation_notes:
Phase A: Sidecar lease store in shard local memory with circular lease table and atomic compare-and-swap for quick reservation. Phase B: Bloom orbit sampling pipeline — use counting bloom to allow deletes with saturating counters. Phase C: Kernel hint plumbing in pinger interface and selection cost table. Phase D: Async reconciler: batch flushes to allocator every 50-200ms with backoff under pressure.

Data structures: lease entries (slot_id, owner_epoch, soft_ttl, warm_flag), orbital bloom (8KB per shard, configurable), per-tenant prefill budgets.

Observability: add metrics: lease_acquire_latency, lease_conflicts, orbit_prefetch_hits, orbit_prefetch_failures, reconciler_batch_size, reconciler_flush_latency, kernel_hint_counts. Traces should annotate decode spans with lease_id and orbit_decision_tag.

Rollout plan: Canary on 10% of shards in perf cluster with synthetic mixed workload. Monitor 99/999 latencies and eviction delta. Gradual ramp to 50% then 100% if stable.

Risks and mitigations: Stale speculative prefills leading to wasted memory — mitigate via tight budget and bloom aging. Lease table can become saturated under pathological microburst — mitigated by admission backpressure and fallback to synchronous allocation for LATENCY_SENSITIVE requests. Kernel hint misuse — provide conservative defaults and telemetry to detect noisy apps.
milestones: 2026-03-08: Prototype sidecar lease table and fast reservation API
2026-03-11: Implement counting bloom orbit sampler and local prefetch worker
2026-03-16: Kernel hint integration and selector mapping for PREFILL_HINT
2026-03-18: Reconciler batch flush and basic telemetry
test_plan:
Unit tests for lease acquire/release semantics, bloom false-positive bounds, reconciler idempotency. Integration test with synthetic traffic mix (short chat vs long generation) verifying warm_flag visibility. Chaos test: simulate lease table overflow and verify fallback to allocator without data loss. Performance microbench harness to measure tail latency and metadata update rate.

Artifacts: perf harness repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/prefill-harness (PR TBD). Design doc draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/slot-lease-sidecar-bloom-orbit
comments: 2026-03-06 - Aisha Kapoor: Spike shows sidecar reduces allocator lock hold time by ~60% in single-shard sim. Need to validate under multi-tenant churn.
2026-03-09 - Marco Li: Implemented basic lease table and counting bloom. Observed bloom false-positive rate ~2.8% at 8KB with current workload; plan to tune counters.
2026-03-11 - Olivia Chen (PM): Prioritize kernel hint defaults so SDKs don't have to change initially. Good to keep PREFILL_HINT invisible to public API.
2026-03-12 - Marco Li: Added metrics and tracing fields. Canary schedule proposed for 2026-03-20 pending perf review.
notes: This approach intentionally trades increased local background IO for fewer synchronous allocation stalls. If orbit proves noisy, we can tighten budgets and increase bloom aging or disable on per-tenant basis. Consider follow-up: persistent lease journaling for fast restarts and cross-shard lease migration if we later want global prefill coordination.
